subject: Ephemeral burn-rate buffer request for 72h POC load run
messages:
From: Joe Alvarez <joe@optimaretail.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: OptimaRetail Procurement <procurement@optimaretail.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: ephemeral burn-rate buffer for 72h POC load run

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We’re scheduled to run a 72-hour latency/throughput validation for the Optima Retail recommendation engine POC on Dec 7–9. Before we start, procurement has asked us to confirm any temporary credits or trial uplift Redwood can provide so we don’t hit hard limits mid-run.

Quick details:
- Goal: validate p95 < 120ms at 12k RPS sustained for ~6h daily windows, with peak bursts to 20k RPS for short intervals.
- Model: optima-reco-v2 (open model variant), sequence len ~128 tokens on average.
- Expected token burn: ~1.1M tokens/hour during peak windows, estimated total ~140M tokens over 72 hours.
- Why we need credits: Our sandbox account has tight default quotas and we need an ephemeral buffer to avoid failed requests and to measure real-world tail latency.

Ask: Can Redwood provision an ephemeral credit buffer equivalent to ~200M tokens (or promotional trial uplift) for the 72-hour window, expiring 48 hours after the run? We prefer credits rather than a monthly quota change.

I’ve attached the test plan (optima_poc_testplan.xlsx) with ramp schedules and telemetry hooks. If you need procurement approval on a DocuSign, let me know and I’ll loop them in.

Thanks — Joe

--
Joe Alvarez
Lead SRE, OptimaRetail
joe@optimaretail.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

- Approve a promo credit voucher for 200M tokens tied to DEAL-2026-487, valid Dec 7 00:00 UTC–Dec 11 23:59 UTC (48h post-run expiry).
- Apply a billing note and mark as ‘non-recurring trial uplift’ in HubSpot.
